messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] AI-Assisted Data Analysis: Modern Workflows - AI workflows for epidemiology
messages.subject_clean: AI-Assisted Data Analysis: Modern Workflows - AI workflows for epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Epidemiological datasets require analytical workflows that remain inspectable from input to output. AI-Assisted Data Analysis: Modern Workflows is a seminar livestreaming October 6 with Kimberly Fessel (Dr Kim Data | Data Science Consultancy). Validate AI-generated Python code before using it to clean, explore, visualise, or analyse epidemiological data. Work with missing values, outliers, descriptive summaries, and charts while keeping statistical reasoning and data privacy central. Apply reproducible workflows to document analytical decisions in R-adjacent epidemiological research practice.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/ai-assisted-data-analysis-modern-workflo
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Multilevel and Mixed Models for Epidemiology
messages.subject_clean: Multilevel and Mixed Models for Epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - A rigorous approach to dependent observations can sharpen epidemiologic inference. Multilevel and Mixed Models with AI is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 7 and 9 with Michael Zyphur (Instats | instats.org). Model clustered patient, clinic, and repeated-measures data by separating within-group from between-group variation. Estimate mixed-effects models in R and Mplus, then diagnose convergence and specification problems. Apply mediation, moderation, and simulation to epidemiologic questions while documenting AI-assisted coding and interpretation.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/multilevel-and-mixed-models-with-ai
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Instats Certifications now Live: Free for Members
messages.subject_clean: Instats Certifications now Live: Free for Members
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI colleagues

Here's a brief update for R-SIG-EPI colleagues on our new Instats certifications in research methods and data analysis, including AI programs alongside causal inference, SEM, multilevel modeling, meta-analysis, machine learning, and qualitative/mixed methods programs (see instats.org/results?view=Seminars&nav=Certifications).

Complete each program's requirements to earn an official, verifiable Instats credential and digital badge that you can add to LinkedIn, include on your CV, and share across your professional network. Each certification offers a focused program of advanced training, with core seminars and electives of your choosing based on their relevance to your research.

An Instats membership gives you unlimited access to all certifications free of charge (instats.org/membership), and if you've already taken the required Instats seminars, these can automatically count toward your certification.

Please feel free to share this with colleagues and students who may be interested.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Data-Driven Methods for Deploying AI - AI deployment diagnostics
messages.subject_clean: Data-Driven Methods for Deploying AI - AI deployment diagnostics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Physical sensing can expose assumptions hidden during model development. Data-Driven Methods for Deploying AI is a seminar livestreaming October 16 with Manish Chauhan (School of Physics, Engineering and Technology, University of York). Quantify simulation-to-real domain shift with divergence measures and diagnose sensor noise, latency, and calibration problems. Apply Bayesian estimation and uncertainty quantification to improve state inference when epidemiological sensing data are sparse or corrupted. Use these diagnostics to support transparent validation of AI systems for wearable and sensor-based health research.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/data-driven-methods-for-deploying-ai
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Your AI is Garbage and How to Fix It (Europe/UK) - AI reliability
messages.subject_clean: Your AI is Garbage and How to Fix It (Europe/UK) - AI reliability
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Epidemiological analysis needs traceable evidence and inspectable computational procedures. Your AI is Garbage and How to Fix It (Europe/UK) is a seminar livestreaming October 15 with Michael Zyphur (Instats | instats.org). Context engineering, source verification, and repeated evaluation help identify where AI-assisted epidemiological analyses can go wrong. Researchers can apply role boundaries, structured handoffs, and acceptance criteria to workflows that retrieve evidence, work with data, or produce statistical outputs. The seminar addresses error propagation across multi-step tasks and ways to inspect results before relying on them.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/your-ai-is-garbage-and-how-to-fix-it-eur
Please circulate this reminder if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

messages.subject_clean: Statistical Foundations of Data Science with R - Epidemiological analysis in R
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Sound epidemiological inference depends on matching statistical methods to the research question. Statistical Foundations of Data Science with R is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 19 and 23 with Centre for Applied Statistics Courses (CASC) (University College London). R-based data summaries, graphical displays, confidence intervals, and regression support transparent analysis of epidemiological data. Participants learn to plan analyses, select significance tests, assess model fit, and make predictions in RStudio. Epidemiology researchers can apply these skills to describe patterns, compare groups, and communicate statistical findings from their studies.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/statistical-foundations-of-data-science

messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - A practical account of how generative AI produces and limits research outputs. Understanding Large Language Models is a seminar livestreaming October 22 with Peter Gruber (Faculty of Economics, USI Universit? della Svizzera Italiana). Assess tokenization, context limits, and stochastic output when considering AI support for epidemiological analysis. Epidemiology teams can use these concepts to judge suitable tasks in R workflows, research writing, and data analysis. Attention to known sources of failure helps researchers weigh generated results before using them in their work.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/understanding-large-language-models

messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Research teams handling health data need clear choices about computational environments. Local LLMs: Private, Free, and Reproducible is a seminar livestreaming October 26 with Peter Gruber (Faculty of Economics, USI Universit? della Svizzera Italiana). Local model installation, model selection, and Python access can support epidemiological analysis without sending sensitive material to external services. Participants examine quantization, context length, hardware requirements, and tools for connecting models to research workflows. The resulting setup can be documented alongside R-based analyses and revisited during revisions or replication work.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/local-llms-private-free-and-reproducible
Full details are available on the Instats seminar page.

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Spatial Statistics in R for Epidemiology
messages.subject_clean: Spatial Statistics in R for Epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Bring principled spatial inference to geographically referenced epidemiological data. Applied Spatial Statistics Using R is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 26 and November 6 with Arnab Hazra (Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur) and Suman Majumder (Indian Statistical Institute). Spatial dependence assessment, variogram modelling, and kriging in R can strengthen analyses of geographically indexed disease data. Participants can examine autocorrelation, fit spatial regression models, and quantify predictive uncertainty rather than treating nearby observations as independent. These methods can support transparent epidemiological inference, mapped risk estimates, and clear reporting for public health research.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/applied-spatial-statistics-using-r
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Modern causal inference methods in R
messages.subject_clean: Modern causal inference methods in R
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Develop clearer grounds for causal claims in epidemiological analyses. Modern Causal Inference Methods (Europe/UK) is a seminar livestreaming October 28 with Michael Zyphur (Instats | instats.org). R workflows for matching, inverse probability weighting, g-computation, and doubly robust estimation support careful analysis of epidemiological data. Participants assess balance, overlap, treatment effect heterogeneity, and the assumptions behind causal estimates. The material can be applied to observational studies, administrative records, and health datasets where interventions were not randomly assigned.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/modern-causal-inference-methods-europeuk
Please circulate this reminder if it is relevant to colleagues or students.

A reminder - Reliable epidemiological analysis depends on decisions that remain visible to the researcher. Build Your Own AI Research Agent is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 29?30 with Leonid Chindelevitch (School of Public Health, Imperial College London).
